posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md:
Is there anyone who has experience with blue dpss lasers from Aixiz? They have blue lasers on ebay from $999 and the seller claims they are suitable for holographic work. I asked if the laser was up to 1 m coherence length (bandwidth 300 MHz or less, linewidth 0.00015 or less. I accidently calculated for 532 nm instead of 473 nm, but it is still in the ball park.) and the seller said yes. The seller also confirms that the laser is suitable for holography regarding long coherence length, single line, Tem00, stable, no mode hopping.

When I asked if I could see some holographic work done with this laser system the seller says several holographic companies, like Holospectra, Integraf, MIT and Purdue all use these systems for this type of use.

If all this is true it is great. A blue dpss for $999 would be many holographers dream coming true.

Someone with experience? What do you think? It would be great if we could test it to see if it works.

[http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?Vi ... :RTQ:US:11](http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&item=110164951736&sspagename=ADME:X:RTQ:US:11)

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Now that I have looked through the website and ebay store I would be cautious. I think this is an importer. Good questions to ask are "Is it single longitudinal mode". And "Can you provide the spectrum output from a spectrum analyzer or scanning Farby-Perot interferometer?"

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
Let me add a further note of caution. Wait until you hear from Integraf, or someone you know, who has used this system for holography.

I think it's very unlikely that it has adequate coherence. (A forum member recently sent me a photo of a DCG hologram he made with a 473nm solid-state laser, which was banded.)

Back in the late 90's, Laser Power introduced that dual-beam blue dpss laser with 5-meter coherence (which later became the Melles 58-BLD-605) and we know the incredible lengths they had to go to, to get that kind of coherence (separating the forward and backward propagating beams, for instance). When I inquired about the price in 1999, they said it was $21,000 for the short coherence-length version, but that the long-coherence length version was an extra $6,000, or $27,000. "Blue noise" is even more notorious than green noise.

Has anyone on this forum used a blue dpss laser (other than the one above) with more than an inch of coherence?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Can you define blue noise? That is not a term I have heard of.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** Can you define blue noise? That is not a term I have heard of.

Not really, Colin, I've never dealt with the issue myself. There has been cryptic mention of the terms "green noise" and "blue noise" in the papers, and I take it to mean (and I could be wrong incidentally) anything that reduces coherence (whatever that may be). But the papers I've read make it pretty clear that "blue noise" is more troublesome than green.

posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md:
Alec Jeong at Integraf replied to my question and said that Aixiz is mistaken. Integraf doesn´t have any of Aixiz blue lasers, though they have tested many of Aixiz red and green diodes for holographic applications, with inconsistent results, but they haven´t tested their blue lasers.

I haven´t got any more substantial information from Aixiz so their claim is probably too good to be true. We probably will have to wait for a long time before an affordable blue laser will turn up for the amateur holographer.
